question: Score-optimal DP density; is the density free to be non-integer?
number: The memory term pins d at the boundary: use the whole 2^20 budget. Table room: (2^20 - 374,400 - 2,048)/32 = 21,004 keys. Non-integer density 2^-113.70 (DP = low 113 bits zero plus a comparison of the next bits, done only in stage 2, 0 extra main-loop ops) gives mean 20,147 finished trails and P(table full) below 1e-9: delta -0.001982 bit (1e-6 tail: d=113.688, -0.002057; 1e-12: d=113.711, -0.001920). With 25 B entries (key 8 + t 2 + length 15 B) 26,885 keys fit: d=113.34, delta -0.003894 bit.
notes: universe cell blake3-r3|GENERIC.DPFRAC|GENERIC|Q3. Requires restating proof Lemma 2 for density 2^-113.7 (trail count 20.1k instead of 16.4k) and the memory ledger. Entry width of 25 B follows from length < 12 x 2^114 (15 bytes) and t < 2^16 (2 bytes) plus an 8 B key; unbuilt. Convention: filed rho.py ledger (research/blake3_r3/candidate_blake3/experiments/rho.py, 125.10856); our copy led() in dig_scan/common.py reproduces total 58516868528290066067270868803654989992793/2 exactly.
